subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Staging, performance status and response assessment

steps.tx: Cancer staging defines the anatomical extent of malignancy, providing a standardised framework for prognosis and treatment selection. The **AJCC/UICC 8th Edition TNM staging** system incorporates anatomical tumour extent, regional nodal involvement, distant metastases, and prognostic molecular biomarkers. Incorporating biological drivers into anatomical staging refines prognostic groupings across breast, prostate, and head and neck cancers.

steps.tx: Patient physiological fitness dictates the feasibility and safety of systemic antineoplastic therapy. The **ECOG performance status** scales functional reserve from 0 for fully active to 4 for completely bedbound, guiding systemic chemotherapy eligibility. Patients with performance status 0 or 1 generally tolerate multi-agent regimens, whereas status 3 or 4 indicates poor tolerance and heightened chemotherapy-related mortality.

steps.tx: **Performance status** describes how well a patient manages daily life and predicts how well they will tolerate treatment. The **ECOG** scale runs from zero, fully active, to four, completely bedbound. The **Karnofsky** score is recorded in steps of ten, with higher scores meaning better function. Both tools are standard in Indian oncology trial and clinic practice.

steps.tx: Objective assessment of solid tumour response under cytotoxic therapy relies on standardised radiological criteria. **RECIST 1.1** defines partial response as at least a 30% decrease and progressive disease as at least a 20% increase in the sum of longest diameters of target lesions. Progressive disease additionally requires an absolute increase of at least 5 mm in the sum, or the appearance of new malignant lesions.

left.title: Complete and Partial Response
items: Complete response: disappearance of all target and non-target lesions
Pathological lymph nodes must decrease to short axis < 10 mm
Partial response: at least 30% decrease in target sum of diameters
Requires baseline target lesion designation up to five total

right.title: Stable and Progressive Disease
items: Progressive disease: at least 20% increase in target sum of diameters
Absolute minimum increase of 5 mm above smallest nadir sum
Appearance of one or more unequivocal new lesions signifies progression
Stable disease: insufficient shrinkage for PR and insufficient increase for PD

steps.tx: Immunotherapy introduces novel radiological patterns of response, including transient tumour flare followed by shrinkage. The **iRECIST** framework addresses immune-checkpoint **pseudoprogression** by requiring confirmation of disease progression 4 to 8 weeks after initial suspected tumour increase. The initial progression is termed unconfirmed progressive disease (iUPD), which transitions to confirmed progressive disease (iCPD) only if repeat scanning demonstrates further tumour growth.

steps.tx: Fluorodeoxyglucose uptake reflects glycolytic activity, providing earlier detection of therapeutic response than anatomical dimensional change. The **PERCIST** criteria evaluate **metabolic tumour response** using fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose PET imaging based on SULpeak measurements in target tumour regions. Partial metabolic response is defined as at least a 30% decline in SULpeak, while progressive metabolic disease requires a 30% increase or new metabolic focus.

rows: Complete resolution of FDG uptake to liver background
>= 30% and >= 0.8 SUL unit decrease in target SULpeak
Neither PMR nor PMD criteria met
>= 30% and >= 0.8 SUL unit increase, or new lesion

steps.tx: Lymphoma staging and post-treatment assessment require tailored criteria integrating metabolic imaging. The **Lugano classification** evaluates lymphoma response using PET-CT and the **Deauville 5-point scale**, where scores 1 to 3 indicate complete metabolic remission. A Deauville score of 1 represents no uptake above background, score 2 represents uptake equal to mediastinum, and score 3 represents uptake between mediastinum and liver.

rows: Uptake markedly higher than liver or new lesion

steps.tx: Intracranial neoplasms exhibit unique radiological features that confound standard dimensional response criteria. The **RANO criteria** assess response in **high-grade gliomas** by combining MRI contrast enhancement, T2/FLAIR non-enhancing infiltration, and clinical corticosteroid requirement. Pseudoprogression occurs within 3 months of completion of temozolomide chemoradiotherapy, characterized by increased enhancement that subsequently stabilizes without altering antitumour therapy.

left.title: RANO Complete & Partial Response
items: Complete response: complete disappearance of all enhancing tumour
Stable or improved non-enhancing T2/FLAIR hyperintensity
Complete cessation of corticosteroids (physiological replacement allowed)
Partial response: >= 50% decrease in sum of enhancing products

right.title: RANO Progression Criteria
items: >= 25% increase in sum of perpendicular enhancing products
Significant increase in non-enhancing T2/FLAIR infiltration
Appearance of any unequivocal new intracranial lesion
Clinical neurological deterioration requiring increased corticosteroids

steps.tx: Hypervascular tumours treated with anti-angiogenic agents often exhibit necrosis without immediate dimensional shrinkage. The **mRECIST** criteria for hepatocellular carcinoma measure viable tumour demonstrating **arterial enhancement** rather than total lesion diameter on dynamic contrast CT or MRI. Viable tumour corresponds to tissue that absorbs contrast during the arterial phase and washes out during the portal venous phase.
